messages.content:
Питання: Can an employer dismiss an employee while the employee is on sick leave?

Еталонна відповідь: General rule — no: Article 40 of the Labour Code prohibits dismissal on the employer's initiative during temporary incapacity for work (except paragraph 5 of Article 40 and full liquidation). But during martial law Article 5 of Law No. 2136-IX allows it, with the dismissal date set to the first working day after the sick leave ends. A complete answer names both.

Відповідь системи: No — an employer may not dismiss an employee on the employer's initiative during that employee's period of temporary incapacity (sick leave), except on the grounds in clauses 5 and 13 of part one of Article 40, and this restriction does not apply in the case of complete liquidation of the enterprise, institution or organisation [2]. The same principle is reflected in ILO Convention No. 158, Article 6(1): temporary absence from work due to illness or injury is not a lawful ground for dismissal [7]. However, the prohibition concerns dismissal at the employer's initiative only — dismissal at the employee's own request during sick leave is not prohibited by labour law, either in peacetime or under martial law [3]. In that case, if the employee has not withdrawn their resignation letter, the employer dismisses them on the date the employee indicated in the letter or after the two-week notice period expires [1].
